relationship_identity_contract: One relationship record links the coherent starting, current, and qualification records for one position thread. Do not pair records by array order or surface proximity. Use a second relationship only for a genuinely separate concurrent position thread. Preserve missingness and speaker ownership; do not manufacture adoption or agreement.

current.role_interpretation: User's current working position on the supply agreement

source_evidence.text: I am leaning toward a one-season, two-region, nonexclusive agreement capped at thirty-five percent of sales, with the cost-linked floor, separate reporting of cosmetic downgrades, and voluntary farm participation.
I will recommend the packing line only if the grant is awarded and the prepayment has capped recovery, crop-failure protection, and no renewal claim.
I will require public language limited to participating farms and regions and set rejection, waste, labor, and concentration thresholds before signing.
I have not resolved whether voluntary participation really protects nonparticipants if cooperative staff, equipment, and reputation begin orienting around the chain.

qualification.role_interpretation: Remaining conditions, counterpressures, or reopen reasons that could change or limit the current position.

source_evidence.text: I have not resolved whether voluntary participation really protects nonparticipants if cooperative staff, equipment, and reputation begin orienting around the chain.
The chain may still treat the first season as an expansion pipeline, and participating farmers may change planting before renewal terms are known.
If the cooperative exits, crop choices, equipment use, buyer expectations, and new status differences among members will not simply return to their prior state.

starting.limitations: A belief is not a decision, and a proposal is not acceptance of its outcome.
starting.role_interpretation: The user's starting position is a mix of attraction to the income stability and hesitation about reorganizing the cooperative around one buyer's specifications, with an undecided stance on whether the resistance protects member autonomy or a small-scale identity.

source_evidence.text: I manage a produce cooperative owned by forty-two small farms.
A national grocery chain has offered a three-year supply agreement that could nearly double our sales and give farmers more predictable demand.
The chain wants uniform varieties, weekly volume commitments, and packaging under a co-branded label.
I am excited by the income stability but worried that we will reorganize the cooperative around one buyer's specifications.
I cannot tell whether my resistance protects member autonomy or protects a small-scale identity that keeps farmers from earning more.
